label: Early copy phase: first two echoed tokens (recall 1-2) in longer sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely at the first two steps after <DEL> (recall_idx 1 and 2, where the input is the echoed orig(0) or orig(1)); recall 1 carries 67% of the mass and recall 2 31%. It is strongest when many outputs remain: rate rises with L, and it is weak or absent for L<=5 (to_go>=4 is a near-equivalent condition). Magnitude is largest at recall 1 and is boosted when the echoed first token is k (all top examples start with k), then falls off at recall 2 and is near zero at recall 3 and later. Token identity otherwise matters little. Never fires in the original phase or on the <DEL> step, and never on the first occurrence of a token (consistent with the input being a repeat). Misses are mostly low-magnitude activations in L=5 sequences; false positives are mostly L=6-7 steps where it stays silent.

issues: Most of the core holds up. The feature fires only in the copy phase (original and delimiter phases are 0% active). Recall 1 holds 67.4% of the activation mass and recall 2 holds 31.3%. Recall 3 and later is under 2%. The dev scores match the report (P 0.855, R 0.885, F1 0.870, mass recall 0.955).

The explanation treats k only as something that makes activations bigger. In fact an echoed k is a separate trigger that ignores the L and position rule. Firing rate when in_tok==k: 99.8% at recall 1 with L=5 (vs 35% for other tokens), 96.5% at recall 1 with L=4, 99% at recall 2 with L=5, and 78% at recall 1 with L=3. At recall 3 or later it is 25% (43% if to_go>=2), vs 0.6% for non-k inputs at those steps. The test misses list shows this directly, e.g. 'k s x c j <DEL> [k:0.36]' at L=5.

The L cutoff in the predicate is a hard threshold, but the firing rate is a smooth ramp. At recall 1 it runs L=4 11%, L=5 38%, L=6 76%, L=7 96%, L=8 99.8%. At recall 2 it runs L=5 11%, L=6 43%, L=7 77%, L=8 93%. So recall 2 at L=6 is a systematic false-positive cell (57% silent), and recall 1 at L=5 is a systematic miss cell (38% active). Saying the feature is 'weak or absent for L<=5' overstates it for recall 1.
'Firing rate rises with L' is only true within recall 1 and 2. Across all steps the rate by L is flat to slightly falling from L=7 to L=9 (0.128, 0.126, 0.117).
'Never fires on the first occurrence of a token' says nothing: copy-phase inputs are never first occurrences, so this follows from 'copy phase only'.
skeptic.revised_label: Early copy phase: fires on the first two echoed tokens (recall 1-2) when many outputs remain, with the rate rising smoothly with L. A separate trigger: an echoed 'k' makes it fire at any length, and sometimes later in the copy phase.
